one_sentence_story: Brain scans show deja vu is not a memory glitch. It is your front brain catching a false alarm on the spot.
so_what_for_you: When a new room feels odd, do not fear your mind is slipping. Your front check hub just caught a twin room plan and kept your facts straight.

jargon_map.plain: Feeling sure you lived a moment before while knowing it is brand new.
jargon_map.analogy: Like an alarm ringing when you can see zero smoke.

jargon_map.plain: Your front brain checking a gut feeling against the real facts.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a clerk checking a receipt when a charge looks wrong.

jargon_map.plain: A new room built on the same floor plan as an old forgotten place.
jargon_map.analogy: Two different cafes with tables and doors in the exact same spots.

jargon_map.plain: Your side brain lobe ringing a match bell with no real memory behind it.
jargon_map.analogy: Thinking you know a stranger just because they wear your friend's coat.
